pr_body:
# Objective

Add support for presenting each UI tree on a specific window and viewport, while making as few breaking changes as possible.

This PR is meant to resolve the following issues at once, since they're all related.

- Fixes #5622 
- Fixes #5570 
- Fixes #5621 

Adopted #5892 , but started over since the current codebase diverged significantly from the original PR branch. Also, I made a decision to propagate component to children instead of recursively iterating over nodes in search for the root. 


## Solution

Add a new optional component that can be inserted to UI root nodes and propagate to children to specify which camera it should render onto. This is then used to get the render target and the viewport for that UI tree. Since this component is optional, the default behavior should be to render onto the single camera (if only one exist) and warn of ambiguity if multiple cameras exist. This reduces the complexity for users with just one camera, while giving control in contexts where it matters. 

## Changelog

- Adds `TargetCamera(Entity)` component to specify which camera should a node tree be rendered into. If only one camera exists, this component is optional.
- Adds an example of rendering UI to a texture and using it as a material in a 3D world.
- Fixes recalculation of physical viewport size when target scale factor changes. This can happen when the window is moved between displays with different DPI.
- Changes examples to demonstrate assigning UI to different viewports and windows and make interactions in an offset viewport testable.
- Removes `UiCameraConfig`. UI visibility now can be controlled via combination of explicit `TargetCamera` and `Visibility` on the root nodes.

## Migration Guide

If the world contains more than one camera, insert `TargetCamera(Entity)` component to each UI root node, where `Entity` is the ID of the camera you want this specific UI tree to be rendered to. Test for any required adjustments of UI positioning and scaling.

```rust
// before
commands.spawn(Camera3dBundle { ... });
commands.spawn(NodeBundle { ... });

// after
let camera = commands.spawn(Camera3dBundle { ... }).id();
commands.spawn((TargetCamera(camera), NodeBundle { ... }));
```

Remove `UiCameraConfig` component from all cameras. If it was used to control UI visibility, insert `Visibility` component on UI root nodes instead.

**Welcome**, new contributor!

  Please make sure you've read our [contributing guide](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and we look forward to reviewing your pull request shortly ✨
I believe this PR could also close https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/5476. Since you could now render it to a texture and render that texture to a world space quad
CI is failing because you need to run rustfmt
I will clean up the examples and figure out why tests are failing in the upcoming few days.

I've discovered that the tests are failing due to nodes not being added to the `UiSurface` if there is no camera set (which is the case in most tests). Arguably, camera-driven UI can require a camera to be rendered. But this would make the changes less backward compatible, which I would prefer to avoid. I will look into a better way to default rendering target, which would allow for a camera-less rendering.
I have something I'm working on I need to finish urgently but once that's done (hopefully finished today), I'll do an in-depth review. These are changes I've really wanted for a long time.

I've reworked it to default to drawing on primary window, instead of searching for the most suitable camera. This allows Taffy nodes to exist even when no camera is set up and brings layout tests back online.

There is a bug I am having troubles with, though. Not every time, but with a roughly 50% chance `split_screen` example panics on start. My informed hypothesis is that `UiCamera` component is not propagated through the children by the time `ui_layout_system` gets to work (which is strange, since I specify execution order between those systems). And since there is no Root Node with no camera set, the camera-less children cause panic when measures get updated. 

I would appreciate ideas around this bug. Otherwise, I'm pretty happy with what I'm bringing to the table.
I added an example of rendering UI to a texture and using it in a 3D world. I don't know how to approach interaction with it though, so this might be better to cover in a separate PR.
Any chance that this can make it to `0.12.1`?
No, 0.12.1 is only for bug fixes. This is a completely new feature.

@bardt 

For the interaction, it's fine for now if it doesn't work. bevy_mod_picking already figured all this out to correctly translate mouse position to 3d position. It will very likely be upstreamed, so for now it's fine if there's no interaction.

@Davier Thank you for reviewing! I will go through all the comments and try to improve the areas you highlighted. 

But let's talk about the big picture first:

> I see that you chose to add a component on every Node to keep track of its camera. Could you comment on this choice, compared to only having a component on the roots?

This PR is inspired and in a lot of ways based on this previous work https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/5892 @oceantume writes in the description the following:

> This comes with a lot of changes to the flexbox code, mainly because each node that's rendered now depends on information that's stored on its root (the scaling factor coming from the render target and viewport) which requires recursive iteration of the nodes instead of a simple query iteration.

I came to the same conclusions, and also noticed that we need access to camera properties when extracting and rendering nodes:
- https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/10559/files#diff-fd92b1243b4cfed68b98f0027f06728c121f50117b01f6a167d2e21511b9663cR659-R669
- https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/10559/files#diff-e9c656d3ddce3547e266352aa46c55185b468838c2eaf40066eb2c15df07d21eR85-R87

So, we need camera information easily reachable via a node. My reasoning is that nodes tree changes relatively rarely in comparison to extraction and rendering, and therefore it would be cheaper to recursively update camera component on nodes than to lookup the corresponding root for each node in extraction.

While writing this, I fought that if there was a quick way to get root node for every node, then we could store the Camera on the root only. Is there such a way?

I also hit the scaling factor issue in #1211, and thought it could be fixed by using logical pixel sizes (but that was blocked on stretch being unmaintained). I do not know at a glance if the new pipelined architecture makes it more difficult.
To be clear, I do not think this question should be blocking the PR, I only wanted it to be addressed 😄

> My informed hypothesis is that `UiCamera` component is not propagated through the children by the time `ui_layout_system` gets to work (which is strange, since I specify execution order between those systems).

That´s probably the case. Commands are not applied automatically after every system, they are deferred. The `apply_deferred` example shows how to force it.
Rather than UiCamera, can we use RenderLayers here?

@JMS55 `RenderLayers` were tried and discussed in one of the previos PRs, and found not the right way forward. You can find the reasoning in this comment and below https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/5414#issuecomment-1198960129
Makes sense, thanks for the context.
Is this still being worked on?
@tygyh I’ve done all I planned, and was waiting for another review. I will resolve conflicts next week.

a couple more future thoughts:
- it would be nice if "pure" ui cameras didn't need to render every frame when their content hasn't changed. i think this is easy enough for users to manage manually so could definitely be done as future work, (if at all). this might be another point for using explicit ui cameras rather than implicit?
- it would be nice to have some way for "pure" ui cameras to resize their targets to the appropriate size for the content. i'm not sure if this can be done already and maybe it's very niche, but it is something i'd like to have personally

probably not for this pr, but i feel like requiring ui roots to be unparented is not helpful anymore. for world space ui i want to attach the ui to the spatial entity that it's rendered on, and now i have to use some separate remote bookkeeping to manage the ui entity. i guess relations will make this easier but it still seems unnecessary.

i would prefer if `UiRoot` was a component instead, and designated a new tree. `TargetCamera` could be an option within it. finding it on a child would stop the child from being included in the hierarchy and make it a new hierarchy instead. for backwards compatibility we could default it on nodes with no parent.

i think this is just a case of changing the queries on the layouting system (edit: and a few other systems which use `Without<Parent>` needed non-trivial changes, to reset `GlobalTransform` and avoid propagating the `TargetCamera`, which i guess means we should also stop using GlobalTransform/Transform for ui positioning which is a much larger change).

> this is great and seems to work well.
> 
> i suspect this pr makes `UiCameraConfig` pretty much obsolete? the only remaining use is if you want to disable ui on your only camera (which you can always do with `Visibility` anyway) ... is it worth keeping around just for that?

IMO we remove this in this PR too.
Done removing `UiCameraConfig`. Added a comment about it to the PR description.

It looks like your PR is a breaking change, but you didn't provide a migration guide.

  Could you add some context on what users should update when this change get released in a new version of Bevy?
  It will be used to help writing the migration guide for the version. Putting it after a `## Migration Guide` will help it get automatically picked up by our tooling.

issue_context.title: Support multiple UI roots
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

In order to support #5570 or #5621 we need a way to define multiple separate UI trees. Each UI root should have data defining which window, viewport and / or render layer they belong to.

> I think the best way of handling it would be to support multiple UI roots with an explicit component that also encodes the settings for the whole tree under the root. This would be one place to specify the `RenderLayer` (or for a better higher level API: specify the camera that renders the UI under the root)

_Originally posted by @nicopap in https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/5414#issuecomment-1199134972_
comments: For context, Draft PR #1211 has plenty of discussion.

review_comments:
bit of a shame to `apply_deferred` here.

could we instead add the `TargetCamera` to `NodeBundle` (and variants) and then mutably update it in `update_target_camera_system`, which would avoid needing to apply commands before layouting?
This `apply_deferred` also smells to me a bit, but I am not super familiar with the technique you are referring to and would ask for an example and probably another opinion here.
This is not blocking, I’ll make a pr for it after merge. I appreciate the effort so far and the dwindling motivation, will re-review and approve shortly so we can get it over the line.
This breaks the example for me, and it may be related to scale factor (I will investigate)

I fount the problem. The camera was rendering into a viewport, but `UiCamera` was not set on root UI node, and it defaulted to rendering into the primary window. This explains misalignment between cursor position and pixels displayed.

Setting viewport on a camera without linking it to the UI root node is an easy mistake to make, and I am not sure what would be an optimal API design to prevent it. At some point I used to default to the first camera rendering to the primary window if no `UiCamera` is set on a node, which would prevent this issue from happening. But then I faced a lot of tests failing without at least one camera existing in the world, and I switched the default from camera to the primary window.

I guess defaulting to a primary window *camera* (as I used to do) with a second fallback to the primary window itself (which I currently do) might be the way to do it.

I will investigate if this second fallback even makes sense, and if rendering UI to the primary window with no camera existing even worked before my changes.

I wonder if it might make to not have a default at all: if you want to render UI then you need to set up a camera / viewport to render into.

> I guess defaulting to a primary window camera (as I used to do) with a second fallback to the primary window itself (which I currently do) might be the way to do it.

When you say "fallback to the primary window", do you mean that you can render UI to a window without going via a camera? I assumed that the way this would work would be that UI would always be camera driven and that "defaulting to the primary window" would just mean "defaulting to the primary camera of the primary window" (which I'm guessing is created automatically?)

Yeah, I realized I don't have a clear picture in my head for what the default behavior should be. So far my driving force in these regards was just trying not to break too much stuff. I've just checked, and before my changes UI did not render without a camera.

I see 2 options now:
1. Make `UiCamera` component required on the root node. Nodes without it would not be rendered. This leads to a clear migration guide, less assumptions in the rendering code, and removes the need for `UiCameraConfig` as one can disable UI by removing `UiCamera` component from the root node. It also adds a little code to all the minimal examples, since one would need to know the camera `Entity` when they instantiate the UI.
2. Make `UiCamera` optional and try to assume the camera to render to. The goal would be to mimic current behavior: set up camera, set up UI nodes, UI is rendered to the camera. This would allow for a minimal boilerplate for simple examples while keeping complex ones configurable. This makes rendering code more complicated though, and the assumptions are potentially non-deterministic (ex. if more than one camera exists, which one should we render to by default?). This behaviour is also harder to explain.

I am gravitating towards *option 1*. 

--- 
Side note and potentially separate discussion. While writing this I realized that approach with `UiCamera` component will not allow us to render the same UI tree to several cameras, as we can now. *Is this a desirable feature?* If so, we may want to either:
1. go the other way around, and replace `UiCameraConfig`with `UiRootNodes(HashSet<Entity>)`
2. change to `UiCamera` to contain `HashSet<Entity>` and render to multiple cameras
Both will mean that in layout and rendering code we would need to account for potentially displaying the same node to views of different size and scale factor.

Is rendering the same UI to more than one view is a desired feature? Or can we accept that if there is a need for such a behavior, one can create 2 identical node trees and render them to different cameras?

We used to have dedicated UI cameras, which I found less confusing than the current situation. It seems they were removed in #4745 "by popular demand", so ergonomics are clearly important.

We could have a compromise between your two options: If only one camera exists, draw UI on it. If more than one camera exist, require all UI roots to select a camera (and warn if any UI root is not displayed because of that).

***

> Is rendering the same UI to more than one view is a desired feature? Or can we accept that if there is a need for such a behavior, one can create 2 identical node trees and render them to different cameras?

I don't think this is desirable. We store some state on the ui entities, like the layout result, the mouse interactions, etc. A lot of these components would not make sense with multiple cameras.

Other suggestion that I actually prefer:
- we separate UI cameras from 2d/3d cameras, into their own marker type `CameraUi`, remove `UiCameraConfig` (and probably rename `UiCamera`)
- the UI plugin automatically spawns a UI camera for the primary window, and marks it at the default UI camera
- UI root nodes that are not assigned a camera use the default one

Advantages:
- exactly same ergonomics as previously for simple cases
- better ergonomics if you have multiple 2d/3d cameras, since there is no need to hide the UI in `UiCameraConfig`s
- UI cameras actually have their own `Camera` component. They don't need to share it with an unrelated camera, so it can be set for its needs (`order`, `viewport`, `output_mode`, ...)
- the UI's `ExtractedView` component lives on the same (render world) entity as its `RenderPhase` (currently the `RenderPhase<TransparentUi>` is on the 2d/3d camera's entity instead). It matters because `RenderCommand`s can only access components on their item's entity and their view's entity. It's a small issue but I stumbled on it today.

Issue:

- from what I remember, the main issue with separate UI cameras was that by default they don't clear the background before rendering (so that the 2d/3d scene is visible). So there is a problem if there are no 2d/3d cameras to clear it at the start of the frame. I don't think it's a difficult one to solve.

I'm aware that it's enough work to be a PR on its own, and probably controversial, but I wanted to write it somewhere and test the waters.

> We could have a compromise between your two options: If only one camera exists, draw UI on it. If more than one camera exist, require all UI roots to select a camera (and warn if any UI root is not displayed because of that).

I like this idea. It will allow for a quick start, further customization, and will not require a significant rethinking of the rest of the work accomplished in this PR. I will implement it and get back with the results.
